title: Amendment of Contracted Particulars on a Corporate Travel Programme
content:
Under the Corporate Travel Programmes, the contracted seat count may be changed within the tier's seat range, and a change outside that range is a tier change rather than an amendment.

| Particular | Whether and where it may be changed | When the change takes effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The contracted seat count, within the tier's seat range | May be amended | From the start of the next billing period where it changes what is billed |
| The contracted seat count, beyond the tier's seat range | Not an amendment but a change of tier | — |
| The invoicing frequency | May be amended at a period boundary only | At that period boundary |
| The payment terms | Only with the corporate desk's agreement, and not at the service desk | — |
| The administrator's address or telephone number | May be changed free of charge | Immediately |

## The invoicing frequency

The invoicing frequency may be changed only at a period boundary, and a change from annual to monthly does not entitle the company to a refund of the annual subscription already charged.

## The payment terms

Payment terms are contractual and are changed only with the corporate desk's agreement; the administrator may not change them at the service desk.

## The administrator's contact details

Changing the administrator's address or telephone number is free and takes effect immediately.

## What an amendment never touches

An amendment never alters the contract term, the negotiated rates or the early exit charge, all of which follow the agreement rather than the account record.

## When an amendment reaches the bill

Where an amendment changes what is billed, the change takes effect from the start of the next billing period and never retrospectively.

An amendment carries, as the case may be, the changed number of contracted seats, the changed invoicing frequency, the changed payment terms and the changed contact address and telephone number of the administrator.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical)

**A company invoiced yearly asks part way through the year to be invoiced monthly instead.** The change is made at a period boundary, and the annual subscription already charged is not refunded to it.

**A company asks the service desk to lengthen its payment terms.** Payment terms are contractual and are changed only with the corporate desk's agreement.

**A company asks for its contracted seats to be raised above its tier's ceiling.** That is a change of tier rather than an amendment of the contracted particulars.

**A company amends its contracted seats in the middle of a billing period.** Where the amendment changes what is billed, it reaches the bill from the start of the next billing period, and nothing is re-billed for periods already run.
